"tulak" and "aka" means "studded" and "leather".

"ul" should means "to/for"

"Maruk goshak tefar pixo ul batuk?" - "Do you want to buy arrows to/for (a) bow?"

Aside from "Mok", any word can be used as NO but I'll use the same word as Amber.

The word "pashak" means "sell", but looks like the Blind Orc don't buy anything.

--Haz 14:00, 6 Apr 2005 (EDT)

Hunter of Dragoes made some strange edit to the page, adding several words not listed before.. I wonder where he got it from, and if they're indeed true

don't have much time so gonna keep my statement to that

 Nagatho Goldenflag 

 Talk   Contributions  13:02, 12 February 2007 (PST)

My words are indeed true. See, please, my translation of some books (Single Books).

<·> Hunter of Dragoes <·> My Talk <·> My Contributions <·> 14:05, 12 February 2007 (PST)

alright, guess I sounded too meany.. just wanted to make sure, 'cause if they really are right, then I wonder why I hadn't heard of any until now... But I've considered that it could be taken out of the Blind Orc Statements by using logical deduction and a bit of sense

well maybe there is some other source for it, but I'll refrain from asking about them this time

sheep hugs,

 Nagatho Goldenflag 

 Talk   Contributions  15:44, 12 February 2007 (PST)

I saw that if you try to buy and you dont have money Blind orc say: Maruk nixda! Maruk is you and nixda is ???. Nixda must be "cant" or "poor" what you think?

-  Kwigon the sharpshooter   Talk   -February-21-2007.

Kwigon the sharpshooter, i am agree with you; "Maruk Nixda!" should means "You Can Not Afford!". What is your opinion about "ba", "ta" and more important "klamuk"? Check this:

Blind Orc: Maruk goshak ta?

Player: nok

Blind Orc: Buta maruk klamuk!

... maybe could be translated to: "you are stupid!"

And, by the way ... If the Hunter of Dragoes words are 100% correct, then why Orc Warlord yells "Ikem rambo zambo! Orc buta bana!" (Now thanks my friend! Orc is slave!) ?

Enjoy your day, 
-  Mithwen   Talk  

Kinda illogical that orcs would call themselves slaves. Most likely "Orc buta bana" means "orcs rule", "orcs are going to make everybody their slaves", or something similar. --Ville-v 09:19, 8 April 2007 (PDT)

Ville-v, the Orcs dominated Rookgaard in the past, but when the Minotaurs  arrived to the island made their slaves. Check the Single Books list, you will found a book titled Rookgaard, Minotaur Hell (on the table)

Enjoy your day, 
-  Mithwen   Talk  

Yes, I did read that book. It only gives overview of history of Rookgaard, but Uldereck's Rock is the strongest kingdom of Orcs, and Orc warlords would definetly not be slaved by minotaurs: Only normal Orcs were dominated, and only on Rookgaard.

Most likely Orc warlord shouts exactly what I did suggest. The "buta bana" may be homophone, and in fact grammar of Orc language may be very different to English.

If you go to foreing country, you don't use grammar of your native language and replace words with ones you look from vocabulary. With some languages that would work, or at least you would be understood, but usually you study most common phrases.

I think Orc Language -page should be competely rewritten to include two parts: Minor vocabulary of orcish given by Amber, and then the logical translations of different phrases. --Ville-v 02:26, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

I am agree with you about "orc buta bana" subject. But, about the grammar of Orc Language ... maybe is too much analisys. Remember, Orcish is a Contructed Language and the correct grammar is unknown. It is very possible that the grammar could be similar to the English or German.

Indeed, rewrite the Orc Language page is a good idea.

Enjoy your day, 
-  Mithwen   Talk

Findings about Orc Language[]

Could somebody tell what exactly does Amber tell about orc language? I don't have any salmon so I cannot test.

I am talking with Blind Orc now:

16:22 Savyl [3]: charach
16:22 Blind Orc: Ikem Charach maruk.
16:22 Savyl [3]: ikem goshak
16:22 Blind Orc: Ikem pashak porak, bata, dora. Ba goshak maruk?
16:23 Savyl [3]: maruk
16:23 Savyl [3]: goshak
16:23 Savyl [3]: goshak donga
16:23 Blind Orc: Maruk goshak ta?
16:24 Savyl [3]: burp
16:24 Blind Orc: Buta maruk klamuk!
16:24 Blind Orc: Futchi.

While saying "Ikem goshak" blind orc responds as human npc does respond to "offer". But real meaning would be "Now buy": "I would like to buy something".

"Goshak" has to be "buy" indeed because it is required to say before item name to buy one.

While answering "burp", which is supposed to be "no", but which exactly sounds like belch, he yells at you: "To be you invader"? Does normal human npc insult you after you say you won't buy item? What if "burp" is some kind of insult, as burping at one's face would be insult in most of cultures?

But... As said above, how can we know "klamuk" is "invader" or "buta" is "to be"? I did read the book translations, and they sound 50% of talking with blind orc and 50% guessing. I would be really interested in what Amber has to say. --Ville-v 06:36, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

And had to add: When one says "hi" to him, he answers "Buta humak!" "To be human"? Most likely not. --Ville-v 06:38, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

This translation seems competely incorrect:

Omark ikem goshak ba batuk
Booz karek utash gort mora
ouk bota bana ikem

Translation:
Got now buy a bow
More dominate gosh people before
we are slave now 

Except the first phrase, the words are found from nowhere, they only have been guessed (according to English word order, even after we have noticed Orcish is more like German). I'll remove all translations of those books, except the shoplist. --Ville-v 07:09, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

"Ikem rambo zambo!" is used by both Blind Orc (as "Good day") and Orc Warlord (as warcry while fighting against humans). Only word known is "Ikem", "now", and we cannot be sure even about it. It is not known if word syntax is German or one Tolkien used in Orcish, so we should get meaning for whole phrase.

What about some phrase which could be used as both greeting to leaving customer, and respecting greeting for opponent who is going to die, such as "Rest in peace", or "See you in Heaven"? I will leave it empty for now --Ville-v 07:34, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Ville-v, you forgot "Maruk nixda!" when you rewrote the Orc Language page. "Maruk nixda!" should be "You can not affort it!"

I am wondering about the word "bata", could be "long" or something like that. Check this ...

"Short Sword" = "Burka"

"Sword" = "Burka Bata" = Longer Short Sword {smiling}

Its only an idea.

Enjoy your day, 
-  Mithwen   Talk  

I didn't forget "maruk nixda", it is in common phrases section. I'll add "burka" as "long". --Ville-v 08:50, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Excuse me but, "bata" should be "long or longer" not "burka". By the way, i am talking with Amber about the Orc Language but need more Salmon {smiling}

Enjoy your day, 
-  Mithwen   Talk  

Could somebody check the books near Bear Room Quest? They seem to have lots of new words and phrases, such as "Orc buta bana" and "Ouk bota bana" instead of usual "Ork buta bana". Either those are typing errors of person who added books to TibiaWiki, or we are dealing with multiple dialects of decaying race, which means translations should only focus around dialect Blind Orc, Amber and inhabitants of Ulderek's Rock use. --Ville-v 08:08, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Ville-v, the text in TibiaWiki is correct but when Hunter of Dragoes translated the Orc's Books near to Bear Room Quest in Rookgaard, replaced "bota" by "buta" before he translated it. Why? Think about that too.

Enjoy your day, 
-  Mithwen   Talk  

Maybe he thought it was typing error of person who wrote the books? But it could be new word as well. I don't think they only added senseless words without thinking first what they would be in German. Maybe I should contact Cipsoft and ask ;) --Ville-v 08:50, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Buta?[]

I suppose when Blind Orc says "Buta humak", he means something like "those humans"...
Art Featherpitch - The mispseller 08:03, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

That is possible. It would sense with "Buta humak" and maybe "Ork buta bana", but not "Fetchi maruk buta" --Ville-v 08:08, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Or maybe it would, because that has been translated incorrectly. "Bye" is "Futchi", and Orc Warlord uses word "Fetchi".

That means we have only three phrases with "buta":

"Buta humak"; "Buta human(s)": Something said to idiot who doesn't understand your language

"Ork buta bana"; "Orc(s) buta ?": Some kind of warcry

"Fetchi maruk buta"; "? you buta": Clearly warcry

What would be logical translation? --Ville-v 08:16, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Then Buta could mean like "damn" or "stupid"? 
Art Featherpitch - The mispseller 14:48, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

That is very likely. And what would be "bana" and "fetchi"? We can guess any insult to phrase "You damned/stupid something."

The same thing is with "bana", we have two phrases:

"Ork buta bana"; "Orc(s) damn/stupid bana"

"Booz karek utash gort mora ouk bota bana ikem"; "? ? ? ? ? ? ? bana now"

Nearly anything fits there. I guess rest of the Orcish will stay unknown unless I succeed to contact Knightmare. --Ville-v 23:01, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Oh wait, we have one more word: "Buta maruk klamuk"; "You damned klamuk". "Klamuk" could mean "paleskin"  or something like that. --Ville-v 00:52, 11 April 2007 (PDT)

maybe an idea

Krakkkk orkkkkkk = Hail Orcs

just a idea
--  Farscaper   Talk   -- 14:54, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Probably. I will add it. --Ville-v 22:46, 10 April 2007 (PDT)

Unless they changed the language i thought 'no' used to be "nok," and 'yes' "mok." Good work so far, i might get involved when i have the time. --DM ><((°> Contribs <°))>< talk to me 17:50, 11 April 2007 (PDT)

Actually any word works as "no" when speaking to the NPC at least, though "nok" is the real word. Some smartass said burp instead and fooled everyone to think thats the real word.
Art Featherpitch - The mispseller - Spam Me 07:42, 12 April 2007 (PDT)

"The Orcish language has been invented long ago. Knightmare does not exclude that some books might have typing errors. However, it´s not possible to translate the Orcish language word by word. This might work for some sentences or for quest relevant key words, but not in general. There used to exist a list with Orcish vocabulary, however, it got lost unfortunately. Therefore I cannot provide you with anything that might clear up the Orcish language." :( --Ville-v 07:39, 13 April 2007 (PDT)

about your interpretation of "Maruk nixda! = You can't afford!":
as cip is german, it might be a small joke. Nixda is kinda slang for "nichts da". translated to english word by word it would mean "nothing there". However, it is used in spoken language as "forget it". For example someone wants to do something and you disagree with his/her idea, you could answer "nixda"/"nichts da". Just an idea, but it would match and fits perfectly. maybe another german can confirm this interpetation as possible.
-- Nolin The Second 06:34, 4 September 2007 (PDT)

Is Amber's Orc Language mission a Quest?[]

Hello all,
I stumbled across the page for Amber, and found that the info on her orc language mission is:

She is one of the few humans who have mastered the Orc Language, and she may be willing to teach you for some of her favorite food.

Seems like there should be more "spoiler" information on her page, such as exactly where to go for the salmon and how to talk to her about it.  Maybe a quest page?  A realize that this page has a sentence on the topic, but that doesn't seem like enough, especially because of the controversial tag...

Thanks Ct 08:47, 16 January 2008 (UTC)

It is a Quest.[]

Yes it is a quest. If you give her salmon she will give you a single orc word.

                                                      -SkullBash (10:54 am)

If you ask blind orc Goshak(buy) the he sees
Blind Orc: Ba goshak maruk? What buy you? and if you ask about
Goshak Bata( buy armor) then he sees Ikem pashak aka bora, tulak bora, grofa. Ba goshak maruk? gives the options and then asks again "what buy you?"

So i guess Ba means what.

Probably, it could also be a verb 'to do' ("do buy you?" or "do you buy?"), however there are a limitless number of possibilities when it comes to things like this, such as grammatical structure and the exact definition of the word, which especially applies to prepositions. Ba could be used in a lot of ways like the English by (example: "I will be done by ten" "this book was written by an orc") or the Dutch van. It would be near impossible to learn an exact translation without a lot of text to analyze, which there isn't -- Sixorish 22:31, 5 February 2009 (UTC)

Tefar[]

Tefar

I have noticed that when you say "Goshak Tefar Pixo", the blind orc sells you 10. However, when you say "Goshak 45 pixo", he will ask if you want to "goshak tefar pixo". More investigation will be done soon.

EDIT: Apparently, and number will get you 10. He only sells arrows in 10s.

Druid or Something (talk) 01:57, June 12, 2014 (UTC)Druid or Something
